title: Constantinople, 381
hook: the council completes the Creed on the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life
carry: the lord and giver of life

segments.voice: Yesterday, pasch: Nicaea's hope that the whole Church would keep the resurrection on one day. Your line was one day, someday.

Read the creed of Nicaea to the end and something is missing. It spends line after line on the Son: God of God, begotten, not made, of one substance with the Father. Then it reaches the Holy Spirit and says only: and in the Holy Spirit. For a while that was enough. Then some teachers began to say the Spirit was less than God: a power God uses, a holy servant, but not Lord. So the bishops gathered again, this time in the emperor's new capital on the water. Today, the council that finished the sentence: Constantinople.
screen: `NICAEA, ON THE SON: LINE AFTER LINE.` → `ON THE SPIRIT: ONE LINE.` → `THE SENTENCE UNFINISHED.`

segments.voice: The Catechism says the faith about the Spirit was confessed at the second ecumenical council, at Constantinople, in 381, and that the creed said at Mass comes from these first two councils together. So the Nicene Creed is really Nicaea, finished at Constantinople. The old Book of Common Prayer gives the added opening like this: "And I believe in the Holy Ghost, The Lord and giver of life." Then, as the Catechism summarizes the council's words: who proceeds from the Father, who with the Father and the Son is worshiped and glorified, who has spoken through the prophets. Take the two titles one at a time. Lord: the same title the creed gives the Son. Not a force, not an energy, not an errand runner. Lord, and worshiped together with the Father and the Son, which the creed would never say of a creature. Giver of life: that reaches back to the first pages of Genesis, where God shapes the man from the earth and "breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul." The Church hears the Spirit in that breath, and Catholics say the one who gave life in the beginning gives life now: in baptism, in prayer, in a dry heart that starts to move again. As the Church tells it, the bishops didn't invent a new teaching. They said out loud what the Church already did when it baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. In the Church's telling: three names, one God, and the third is not an afterthought.
screen: `NICAEA, FINISHED AT CONSTANTINOPLE.` · `LORD: NOT A FORCE.` · `THE BREATH OF LIFE IN GENESIS.` · then, large: `THE LORD AND GIVER OF LIFE.` · then: `THE THIRD NAME, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT.`

segments.voice: Breathe slowly, noticing that this breath came without your deciding and the next is already on its way: on the in-breath, the Lord; on the out-breath, and giver of life. If you pray, use the short traditional prayer, Come, Holy Spirit, and then stay quiet; if you don't, let the breath itself be enough to notice.
Constantinople. The city of the second ecumenical council, where the creed was finished with the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life. Today's word.
Your line: the lord and giver of life. The creed's sentence, finished at last. That's seven hundred seventy-one days.

howItsDone: Catholics say the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed at Sunday Mass and may begin prayer or work with Come, Holy Spirit; the Spirit is invoked at every baptism and confirmation.

chat.says: Why does the Creed say so much more about the Holy Spirit than Nicaea did?

Nicaea forgot the Spirit, and a later scribe filled the gap on his own.
Constantinople wanted a longer creed to sing on the great feast days.
chat.meaning: When some taught the Spirit was less than God, the bishops at Constantinople confessed him Lord and giver of life, worshiped with the Father and the Son.

notes: CCC 245 gives the second ecumenical council at Constantinople in 381; CCC 195 says the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed stems from the first two councils (325 and 381). The year in voice rests on these.
The creed of Nicaea ending 'And in the Holy Ghost' (followed by anathemas) is paraphrased as 'and in the Holy Spirit. Full stop.'; confirm the anathemas don't make this misleading.
'Some teachers began to say the Spirit was less than God' refers to the Pneumatomachians/Macedonians without naming them; confirm.
The BCP 1662 quote stops before 'Who proceedeth from the Father and the Son', since the Filioque was not in the creed of 381 (CCC 247). The council's additions are paraphrased.
'Emperor's new capital on the water' for Constantinople: confirm.
'Come, Holy Spirit' offered as a short traditional prayer (from the Veni Sancte Spiritus tradition); not a new prayer. Confirm.
Editor pass: 'Full stop' cut (the 325 creed goes on to its condemnations); 'didn't invent a new teaching' framed as the Church's own account.

Second editor pass: 'which you would never say of a creature' changed to 'the creed would never say', and the practice no longer tells the listener their breath was 'given to you' (narrator was supplying the belief).
